text_blocks.snippet: In Utah, [Highlight start] homeowners insurance generally covers a roof leak only if it results from a sudden, accidental event ("covered peril") [Highlight end] —such as hail, high winds, or a falling tree—rather than age, wear and tear, or poor maintenance.
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] homeowners insurance generally covers a roof leak only if it results from a sudden, accidental event ("covered peril") [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Sudden storm damage: Leaks caused by wind uplift, hail impact, or storm-created openings.
Resulting interior & contents damage: Water damage to ceilings, walls, insulation, or personal belongings caused by a covered roof event (subject to your deductible and policy terms).
Reasonable emergency mitigation: Temporary protection (like tarping) to stop active water intrusion, as long as you document it and follow policy rules.
Wear and tear or aging: Cracked/worn shingles, deteriorated flashing or pipe boots, or roofs past typical age thresholds (often 15–20+ years, depending on the insurer and roof type).
Gradual or long-term leaks: Slow leaks that have been dripping over months or stem from deferred maintenance.
Flooding / runoff: Outside ground or surface water/runoff generally requires separate flood coverage.
Roof age & valuation: Insurers may scrutinize older roofs or apply Actual Cash Value (ACV) vs. Replacement Cost Value (RCV) depending on policy terms.
Townhomes & condos: Check whether exterior/roof coverage and deductibles fall under an HOA master policy or your individual policy.

text_blocks.snippet: For practical steps on documenting damage, mitigating water inside, and working with an adjuster in Utah, see the Emergency Roof Repair Guide for Utah Homes from Big West Roofing. You can also review general coverage rules for interior belongings and repairs in Harris Balcombe's guide on roof leaks .
